_note: Data-claim manifest — the single source of truth for the book's governed data cross-references. One entry per grounded datum. A `[data: <slug>]` marker in the prose resolves against this file to a footnote-style cross-ref into the chapter that reports the number (fail-loud on an unknown slug, like an unknown {{token}}). Fields: `source` = the chapter slug (a book/<slug>.html page) that reports the datum; `anchor` = the {#heading-id} on that chapter's reporting section ("" until the render lands); `holds` = the load-bearing numbers/units that MUST still appear in the source (the check_data_claims lint compares digit-sequences+units under a loose match; a number change fails, a spelling change is fine; [] until the render pins them); `status` = final | preliminary | partial (the strength signal); `gloss` = a one-line description of the datum. THE ARGUMENTATIVE CHAIN (W-LEDGER 260803): every datum also carries `spine_claim` (or `spine_claims: []` when it genuinely bears weight for more than one) = the argument-spine claim id this number bears weight for (joins to book-models/argument_spine_declared.json — DL1); `observable` = the real-world quantity actually observed; `data_source` = how/where measured, with provenance (tool + method + artifact/commit); `limitation` = what the datum CANNOT show / the honest caveat. A preliminary datum with a stated limitation is honest; an unbound number is not. The extended check (DL1 join-integrity, DL2 four-fields-present, DL3 underquantified report, DL4 holds-still-appear) runs audit-only. The substantiation aggregator (`catalog.py substantiation`) joins these data-claims + the lit-positioning citations under each spine claim to flag under-substantiated-or-situated reality-claims. Regenerate the anchors + this file together when a source section moves. Queryable via `catalog.py data-claims`.

refactor-cost.observable: files touched + lines rewritten + wall-clock for one cross-format migration.
refactor-cost.data_source: An agent-run cross-format migration on the DocAble repo, measured from the landing commit's diffstat and the agent session's wall-clock log.
refactor-cost.limitation: One migration on one repo; wall-clock is agent time, not human-equivalent effort; not a controlled before/after against a hand-refactor baseline.
refactor-cost.gloss: A cross-format migration touched fifty-eight files and rewrote five thousand lines in about five hours of agent time — refactoring became an afternoon's work.

nearly-free.observable: Per-document remediation cost across three sources: do-it-yourself professor time, external-vendor per-page quote, and the tool's per-deck processing cost.
nearly-free.data_source: The DocAble cost model — measured per-deck processing cost (tokens + compute) set against published vendor per-page quotes and a DIY hours-per-document estimate (the book's canonical figures in metrics.json).
nearly-free.limitation: Cost-model estimates, not audited invoices; per-deck cost excludes amortized development; quality-parity with vendor output is asserted, not independently graded.
nearly-free.gloss: The per-document remediation cost cascade — do-it-yourself professor cost vs. external-vendor quote vs. the tool's per-deck processing cost — showing high-quality remediation nearly for free.

velocity.observable: Commits per week across the project's history.
velocity.data_source: A repo-activity histogram over the parent repo's git history (commits metric), 20 weeks from 2026-03-12 to 2026-07-29 (metrics.json _commit_provenance).
velocity.limitation: Commit count is a coarse activity proxy, not delivered value; the count mixes agent, human, and generated commits; single project, single fleet.
velocity.gloss: The velocity curve: commits per week across the project's history, rising as the fleet acquired capability then dipping during hardening.

mbse-nav-token.observable: Tokens-to-answer with MBSE navigation guidance ON versus OFF, across four modeled tasks.
mbse-nav-token.data_source: A controlled A/B pilot (N=4 modeled tasks); tokens-to-answer measured per task with guidance toggled, accuracy graded per answer.
mbse-nav-token.limitation: N=4 pilot — not powered; single fleet; measures tokens, not accuracy (zero accuracy loss noted, but at small N); the system-level Garden-null reframe of the MBSE ablation is coming in W5.
mbse-nav-token.gloss: A controlled A/B pilot of MBSE navigation guidance (N=4 modeled tasks): tokens-to-answer with guidance ON vs. OFF, saving -20% / -12% / -82% / -50%, median ~-35%, zero accuracy loss.

support-ratio-curve.observable: Support-apparatus LoC divided by production LoC at four dated commits (prototype / mechanization / hardening / now): 0.85 -> 2.48 -> 3.68 -> 3.06.
support-ratio-curve.data_source: A categorized line-count tool (run-cloc) with today's category map applied to four historical worktrees via ADA_CLOC_SCAN_ROOT (contamination-free /tmp clone, tool files never inside the counted tree); SHAs c55f3637 (prototype 04-09), e0f10aea (mechanization 05-31), b1a4c1d4 (hardening 06-30), 07af718a (now 08-03).
support-ratio-curve.limitation: LoC is a coarse proxy for effort; ~20% by-design side-trees (root configs, assets, non-primary tests, the book itself) sit outside the census; single-repo, single-author-fleet — a revealed preference, not a controlled comparison of governed vs. ungoverned development. The final-window dip is production growing faster (+45%), not support falling (still +21%). Render location + holds pins land in W4.
support-ratio-curve.gloss: The support-ratio curve across four windows (0.85 -> 2.48 -> 3.68 -> 3.06): governance investment led and kept pace with the fleet, crossing from sub-parity to ~3x while production LoC grew ~47x — the build-the-environment-first revealed preference.

model-sync-efficacy.observable: The model-sync sensor's drift-detection readings and the reconciliation labor they drive: a derived-floor churn of +8,970 / -173 lines over 63 commits with 0 reopens, and a first before-data report of ~27 findings at a signal-to-noise near 1.0.
model-sync-efficacy.data_source: The model-sync measurement (draft committed f6147fc); the §3.8 integration lands in W7. Figures from the sync report's churn ledger + the first drift-detection report's finding tally.
model-sync-efficacy.limitation: A single subsystem's sync episode, before the drift-detector's signal-to-noise was tuned; the ~27-finding S:N~1.0 is a before-data snapshot, not a steady-state rate; not a controlled comparison against un-synced development. Primary binding is the drift-detection (alignment) claim; it also bears on the sync-cost-reduced (co-evolution economics) claim — see the parked-binding note in the results log.
model-sync-efficacy.gloss: The model-sync measurement: a drift-detection sensor whose readings (derived-floor churn +8,970/-173 over 63 commits, 0 reopens; ~27 findings at S:N~1.0 before tuning) show reconciliation stays cheap and divergence is caught.

mmm-drain.observable: The Missing-Model-Metric orphan rate (share of tests whose exercised code reaches no model-anchored symbol) draining as subsystems get modeled: 56% -> 55% -> 52% -> 39% -> 32.2% -> 30.1% -> 20.9% -> 14.9%.
mmm-drain.data_source: A code->model tracer (the MMM pilot tracer, trace.py) re-run over the dispatch/orchestration test population (~144-148 tests) after each model-loop Epic modeled the biggest remaining orphan cluster; sources in the missing-model-metric Epic docs + STRATEGY.
mmm-drain.limitation: The population denominator drifts 144->148 across runs, and the first (56%) point was subsystem-scoped — comparable, not a fixed-N series; the cost-rollup cluster's exact landing point is not separately enumerated. A fixed-N reproducible replay is parked (see results log). Render + holds pins land in W4.
mmm-drain.gloss: The Missing-Model-Metric drain: orphan (code-unmodelled) rate falling from 56% to 14.9% as the model-loop modeled each biggest orphan cluster in turn — code-to-model coverage rising to ~85%.

churn.observable: Per-path additions and deletions (web/ and backend/) across the four study windows; mechanization is the churn peak for both, then deletions collapse and later windows go net-additive (backend/ -286K deletions at mechanization -> -3.8K at hardening).
churn.data_source: git log --numstat scoped per path over the parent repo (2026-03-12 -> 2026-08-03), split into the four study-v2 commit-date windows (re-runnable commands in the w4-data scratchpad).
churn.limitation: Add/delete counts include generated, bundle, and vendored files — a churn/velocity signal, not hand-authored SLOC, and not a clean measure of wasted rediscovery/undo/reconcile effort; a bundle-excluding pathspec would tighten it (parked). Series render + holds pins land in W4.
churn.gloss: Path churn (web/ + backend/) across four windows: mechanization is the add-and-delete peak; later windows go net-additive as the built environment stabilizes the code.

control-growth.observable: The count of governance controls in the tree at four dated windows — project-specific lint files (0 -> 336 -> 595 -> 747) and gate scripts (0 -> 20 -> 76 -> 102) — with 993 registered lint specs at the final window, plus the failure-attribution discipline's footprint: 208 commits carrying a paired fix-and-lint tag and 27 lints citing a specific dated incident in their own text.
control-growth.data_source: A tree scan (git ls-tree per window SHA) counting lint-* files under the lint directory and gate scripts, at the four study-v2 commit-date boundaries c55f3637 (prototype 04-09) / e0f10aea (mechanization 05-31) / b1a4c1d4 (hardening 06-30) / HEAD (now 08-03); registered-spec count from the lint-registration modules at HEAD; the 208 fix-and-lint commits and 27 incident-citing lints from a commit-message and lint-docstring grep (w4b-measurements scratchpad).
control-growth.limitation: A control-growth curve, not a causal rate: the telemetry that would record the fire->control edge captured only the reflection hook firing (event/ts/session/facet), never the resulting control, so the fraction of controls born from a failure versus authored up front is not measured. Attribution is a documented, named discipline (the paired fix-and-lint tag in 208 commits; 27 lints citing a dated incident), reported as an honest range (27 high-confidence -> 260 loose keyword proxy), not a precise causal percentage. Single repo, single fleet; counts are at HEAD 700533b6 / 2026-08-03 and drift upward on re-run.
control-growth.gloss: The control substrate accumulating across four windows: project-specific lint files 0 -> 336 -> 595 -> 747 and gate scripts 0 -> 20 -> 76 -> 102 (993 registered lint specs at the final window), the environment converting failures into durable machinery as a documented, named, growing discipline.
